node-1.label: Mildly pruritic erythematous gradually enlarging lesion on the proximal left calf for 2 years

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his early 70s; the lesion appeared without identifiable cause.

node-3.label: For the previous 2 months, the patient applied topical corticosteroids and antifungals with no improvement.

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed an ill-defined, nonindurated, erythematous-violaceous plaque, slightly raised but with an atrophic appearance.

why.why: Histopathology shows band-like dermal vascular proliferation with CD34/CD31 positivity and D2-40 negativity and no lymphoid atypia. Both experts interpret these findings as refuting cutaneous lymphoma; the T-cell clonality panel is still pending, so a small residual lymphoma possibility remains. The malignant component is now better captured by the specific Kaposi sarcoma hypothesis. Confidence reduced from 0.55 to 0.10.

Histopathology demonstrates a vascular proliferation rather than an inflammatory infiltrate, and expert analyses state that inflammatory etiologies are essentially excluded; the lesion also did not respond to topical corticosteroids. Confidence reduced from 0.15 to 0.02.

Histopathology demonstrates a vascular proliferation, and expert analyses state that fungal etiology is essentially excluded; the prior lack of response to topical antifungals further refutes this hypothesis. Confidence reduced from 0.10 to 0.01.

Although the clinical appearance was atrophic, biopsy reveals a vascular proliferation; expert analyses support a vascular neoplasm, making a primary atrophic skin disease unlikely. The atrophic appearance is likely secondary to the vascular process. Confidence reduced from 0.20 to 0.05.

node-9.label: Biopsy shows band-like dermal vascular proliferation with round vascular channels lined by bland endothelial cells

node-10.label: Immunohistochemistry is CD34/CD31 positive and D2-40 negative

node-11.label: Biopsy shows no hemosiderin deposition or lymphoid atypia

node-12.label: HHV8 immunostaining has not yet been performed

node-13.label: T-cell clonality panel result is not yet available

attrs.why: The elderly patient's chronic violaceous atrophic calf plaque and biopsy showing band-like dermal vascular proliferation with CD34/CD31 positivity and D2-40 negativity are most consistent with Kaposi sarcoma; the pathologist identifies it as the most plausible vascular neoplasm. Confidence is 0.45 because HHV8 immunostaining is pending and bland endothelial cells without hemosiderin also allow a benign vascular proliferation.

The laboratory physician interprets the bland endothelial cells, absence of hemosiderin/lymphoid atypia, and vascular immunophenotype as favoring a benign vascular proliferation. However, the chronic progressive clinical course and lack of response to topical therapy make a benign process less likely than Kaposi sarcoma, so confidence is 0.25.
